title: Fidelity adaptation: evaluation, rollback backstop, and simulation manifest
author: Aisha K. Patel
content:
Overview
========
This document defines the fidelity-adaptation evaluation manifest and the operational backstop policies used when runtime adapts model fidelity (quantized variants, model variants, or batching/caching induced fidelity changes). It specifies: goals, evaluation metrics and thresholds, a canary/simulation protocol, rollback/backstop criteria, required observability signals, and example configuration snippets used by the Runtime Orchestrator.

Goals and scope
----------------
- Keep Redispatch/Degradation events safe for production customers while meeting cost and latency objectives.
- Provide a reproducible simulation and canary matrix so model-variant or quantization rollouts can be verified prior to wide release.
- Define automatic backstops for fidelity regressions that protect SLOs (quality and latency) and allow rapid operator intervention.
- Scope: applies to hosted, dedicated, and private runtime deployments where automatic fidelity adaptation is enabled. Does not replace model-level release QA.

Definitions and acronyms
------------------------
- Fidelity adaptation: any runtime action that may change perceived output quality (e.g., switching to a quantized kernel, using a smaller model-variant, applying aggressive KV-prefetching that truncates context).
- RAR (Relative Acceptance Rate): production A/B style metric estimating fraction of responses accepted by downstream classifiers or human raters relative to baseline.
- Delta-Q: normalized quality delta computed from a weighted combination of evaluation metrics (embedding cosine, task-specific metric, and RAR). Expressed in percentage points.
- Backstop policy: an automated control that pauses rollouts and reverts routing when a Delta-Q or other trigger exceeds thresholds.

Key SLOs and thresholds
-----------------------
- Latency SLO (p50/p95/p99): must not regress by more than 10ms / 30ms / 75ms relative to baseline variant during canary.
- Cost target: expected per-token compute cost reduction >= 7% (measured over 24h sample) for the candidate to be considered.
- Delta-Q backstop: immediate rollback if Delta-Q <= -1.5% (meaning quality drop > 1.5 percentage points relative to baseline).
- RAR backstop: immediate rollback if production RAR delta <= -2.0%.
- Soft alert: if Delta-Q between -0.5% and -1.5% raise P1 but continue canary under operator supervision.

Evaluation matrix (canonical signals)
------------------------------------
- Offline harness: microbench evaluation on canonical prompt-sets (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks). Metrics: embedding cosine to baseline (>= 0.985 for small quant changes), task-specific accuracy (e.g., exact-match), ROUGE-L / BLEU where applicable.
- Shadow traffic comparison: mirror 2% of live traffic for 48 hours; compute latency quantiles, RAR, and token-cost.
- Live canary: gradual traffic ramp 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% over 24–72 hours with active monitoring windows.
- Synthetic surge test: run 2x expected peak for 30 minutes using service load generator and record tail-latency and kernel error rates.

Canary rollout protocol (step-by-step)
-------------------------------------
1. PREP: Validate offline harness (unit tests, integration tests) and produce a canary-report artifact with metrics. Attach artifact to canary change.
2. SHADOW: Enable shadowing on a 2% mirrored slice for 48 hours. Ensure no kernel-level exceptions and collect RAR and Delta-Q.
3. STAGED RAMP: If shadow ok, open staged ramp: 0.5% for 2 hours -> 2% for 12 hours -> 10% for 24h. During ramp: automated checks run every 5 minutes.
4. VALIDATE: At each stage validate: 1) Delta-Q > -0.5%, 2) latency p99 within threshold, 3) kernel failure rate < 0.01%. If any check fails, trigger immediate rollback.
5. GRADUAL RELEASE: If 10% sustained for 24h with no soft alerts, schedule controlled release to 50% with operator approval.
6. FULL RELEASE: After 72h at 50% with evaluations stable, release to 100% or integrate into tiered routing.

Rollback and backstop actions
----------------------------
- Immediate automatic rollback triggers: Delta-Q <= -1.5% OR RAR delta <= -2.0% OR kernel fatal errors > 0.1% over 10 minutes.
- Soft stop: pause ramp and notify on-call if Delta-Q between -0.5% and -1.5%.
- Manual backstop: operator can enact a targeted routing policy that pins affected customers to baseline model-variant for up to 30 days while investigation occurs.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments: follow local operator rollback steps in addition to control-plane backstop; see "deployment-guides" for customer-specific rollback playbooks.

Observability and telemetry requirements
---------------------------------------
All canary runs must emit the following telemetry to the observability pipeline with these minimum cardinalities:
- Per-variant: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token CPU/GPU time, kernel invocation count, kernel error code histogram.
- Quality signals: embedded cosine distribution, RAR estimate, sampled human feedback tags (if available).
- Resource signals: GPU occupancy, GPU memory high-water, NUMA imbalance score, NVLink error counters.
- Control traces: request provenance tag including canary-id, variant-id, kernel-subtype, and sampling decision.

Alerting rules (examples)
------------------------
- Canary-DeltaQ-Critical: Delta-Q <= -1.0% sustained for 3 evaluation windows (5m) -> Pager -> auto-rollback.
- Canary-Latency-Tail: p99 increase > 50% compared to baseline for 10m -> Notify SRE and stop ramp.
- Kernel-Exception-Rate: kernel errors > 0.05% over 5m -> Create incident, auto-fallthrough to fallback kernel.

Simulation manifest (reproducible experiments)
--------------------------------------------
This section contains the canonical experiments and parameters used by the benchmarking lab to simulate production outcomes. Use the following YAML snippet as the manifest input to the experiment runner. Save results to the artifacts bucket with canary-id tags.

Example manifest (YAML, used by sim-runner)
-------------------------------------------
apiVersion: v1
kind: FidelitySimulation
metadata:
  name: "sim-fidelity-{{canary-id}}"
spec:
  duration: 48h
  traffic_profile: "customer-mix-v3"
  mirror_fraction: 0.02
  metrics:
    - name: "DeltaQ"
      computation: "weighted(embedding_cosine:0.6, task_metric:0.3, RAR:0.1)"
    - name: "CostPerToken"
  workload_overrides:
    sequence_length: {p50: 96, p95: 512, p99: 1024}
  failure_injection:
    kernel_pause_rate: 0.0001
    nvlink_degradation: false

(When running, replace templated fields and attach the generated artifact to the canary change.)

Runtime config example (JSON used by Orchestrator)
--------------------------------------------------
{
  "variant_id": "quant128-int8-v2",
  "canary_id": "canary-2026-01-13-q128",
  "routing": {"initial_fraction": 0.005, "stages": [0.005, 0.02, 0.1]},
  "backstop": {"delta_q_threshold": -0.015, "rar_threshold": -0.02, "kernel_error_threshold": 0.001},
  "observability_tags": ["fidelity-canary", "team-runtime"]
}

Operator runbook (quick checklist)
---------------------------------
1. Verify canary-report artifact is attached to change.
2. Start shadow run and confirm no kernel critical errors in first 30m.
3. Approve staged ramp on green signals.
4. Monitor Canary-DeltaQ-Critical and Kernel-Exception-Rate dashboards every 5m.
5. If rollback triggered: pin affected customers, create incident with tag lifecycle:fidelity-backstop, and run regression-huntbook.

Investigation playbook (post-backstop)
-------------------------------------
1. Triaging: collect artifacts (shadow diffs, sampled responses, kernel traces, GPU metrics).
2. Localize: is the regression correlated to sequence-length, prompt pattern, or tenant? Use cohort-labels in traces.
3. Reproduce: run targeted offline sim using the canary-id and failing cohort parameters.
4. Patch: either revert quantized kernel, adjust kernel launch parameters, or tighten routing.
5. Re-run canary with conservative thresholds and extended shadowing.

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- Runtime fidelity experiments are owned by the Serving Runtime team. Primary owners: Aisha K. Patel (runtime experiments), Marco Li (observability), Priya Shah (benchmarking).
- All changes that affect fidelity must include: offline harness report, simulation artifact URL, and a canary plan.
- Monthly fidelity review: automated summaries of all fidelity-adaptation canaries (success/fail/rolled-back) are presented at the Runtime Quality sync.

FAQ and gotchas
---------------
Q: How do we avoid noisy RAR estimates on low-traffic tenants?
A: Use cohort aggregation and require a minimum sample size (n >= 200 requests) before evaluating RAR-sensitive backstops.

Q: What if the quantized kernel shows better RAR but worse p99 latency?
A: Favor user-facing quality SLOs; if latency breach is transient, evaluate kernel-tuning knobs (batch-slicer, prefetch window). If sustained, revert and open a perf-tuning ticket.

Appendix: example monitoring queries
-----------------------------------
- Delta-Q rolling window (5m): avg(weighted_embedding_cosine*0.6 + task_metric*0.3 + rar*0.1) by variant_id
- Kernel error rate: sum(kernel_errors)/sum(kernel_invocations) by variant_id over 5m
